passages.title: Matthew Ridgway
passages.text: General Matthew Bunker Ridgway (March 3, 1895 – July 26, 1993) was the 19 Chief of Staff of the United States Army.

passages.title: Matthew Ridgway
passages.text: He served with great distinction during World War II, where he was the Commanding General (CG) of the 82nd Airborne Division, leading it in action in Sicily, Italy and Normandy, before taking command of the newly formed XVIII Airborne Corps in August 1944, holding this post until the end of the war, commanding it in the Battle of the Bulge, Operation Varsity and the Western Allied invasion of Germany.

passages.title: Allied invasion of Italy
passages.text: The Allied invasion of Italy was the Allied amphibious landing on mainland Italy that took place on 3 September 1943 during the early stages of the Italian Campaign of World War II.

passages.title: Allied invasion of Italy
passages.text: The operation was undertaken by General Sir Harold Alexander's 15th Army Group (comprising General Mark W. Clark and General Bernard Montgomery's British Eighth Army) and followed the successful invasion of Sicily.

passages.title: Allied invasion of Italy
passages.text: The main invasion force landed around Salerno on 9 September on the western coast in Operation Avalanche, while two supporting operations took place in Calabria (Operation Baytown) and Taranto (Operation Slapstick).

passages.title: Operation Epsom
passages.text: Operation Epsom, also known as the First Battle of the Odon, was a British Second World War offensive that took place between 26 and 30 June 1944, during the Battle of Normandy.

passages.title: Operation Epsom
passages.text: The offensive was intended to outflank and seize the German-occupied city of Caen, an important Allied objective, in the early stages of Operation Overlord, the Allied invasion of north-west Europe.

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder
passages.text: Marshal of the Royal Air Force Arthur William Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder, {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (11 July 1890 – 3 June 1967) was a senior Royal Air Force commander.

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder
passages.text: He was a pilot and squadron commander in the Royal Flying Corps in the First World War and he went on to serve as a senior officer in the Royal Air Force during the inter-war years when he served in Turkey, Great Britain and the Far East.

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder
passages.text: During the Second World War, as Air Officer Commanding RAF Middle East Command, Tedder directed air operations in the Mediterranean and North Africa, including the evacuation of Crete and "Operation Crusader" in North Africa.

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder
passages.text: His bombing tactics became known as the "Tedder Carpet".

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder

passages.title: Arthur Tedder, 1st Baron Tedder

passages.title: Loop of Henle

passages.title: Low pressure receptors

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: Identity control theory is a theory in sociology concerned with the development of personal identity.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: Created by Peter Burke, it focuses on the nature of peoples' identities and the relationship between their identities and their behavior within the realm of their social structure.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: The identities of the individual are rooted in their social structure.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: Identity Control Theory was created based on traditional symbolic interaction views where people choose their own behaviors and how their behaviors correspond to the meanings of their identity.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: One of the main aspects ICT deals with is how individuals view their own identities and respond to the reactions to their identities of those around them.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: When an individual is acting according to the identity control theory they reflect on the identity they display and how others approve or disapprove of their identity.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: If the individual does not like the responses of others they will look at how they can change their views of their identity or their identity towards themselves to produce a positive outcome.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: One of the main benefits of this theory is how negative feelings can be prevented by individuals and by those around them.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: The people around someone who is displaying a certain identity have the ability to be more sensitive and prevent negative feelings if they understand identity control theory because they know what will bring out a negative response.

passages.title: Identity control theory
passages.text: On the other hand, the individual can prevent negative feelings that coincide with the teachings of identity control theory if they understand these teachings and can apply them to their own lives.

passages.title: Alternative rock
passages.text: Alternative rock (also called alternative music, alt-rock or simply alternative) is a style of rock music that emerged from the independent music underground of the 1980s and became widely popular in the 1990s.

passages.title: Alternative rock
passages.text: In this instance, the word "alternative" refers to the genre's distinction from mainstream rock music.

passages.title: Alternative rock
passages.text: The term's original meaning was broader, referring to a generation of musicians unified by their collective debt to either the musical style or simply the independent, DIY ethos of punk rock, which in the late 1970s laid the groundwork for alternative music.

passages.title: Alternative rock
passages.text: At times, "alternative" has been used as a catch-all description for music from underground rock artists that receives mainstream recognition, or for any music, whether rock or not, that is seen to be descended from punk rock (including some examples of punk itself, as well as new wave, and post-punk).

passages.title: List of rock genres
passages.text: This is a list of rock music genres consisting of subgenres of popular music that have roots in 1940s' and 1950s' rock and roll, and which developed into a distinct identity as rock music in the 1960s, particularly in the United Kingdom and the United States.

passages.title: List of rock genres
passages.text: By the late 1960s, a number of identifiable rock music subgenres had emerged, including hybrids like blues rock, folk rock, country rock, and jazz-rock fusion, many of which contributed to the development of psychedelic rock influenced by the counter-cultural psychedelic scene.

passages.title: List of rock genres
passages.text: New genres that emerged from this scene included progressive rock, which extended the artistic elements; glam rock, which highlighted showmanship and visual style; and the diverse and enduring major subgenre of heavy metal, which emphasized volume, power, and speed.

passages.title: List of rock genres
passages.text: In the second half of the 1970s, punk rock both intensified and reacted against some of these trends to produce a raw, energetic form of music characterized by overt political and social critiques.

passages.title: List of rock genres
passages.text: Punk was an influence into the 1980s on the subsequent development of other subgenres, including new wave, post-punk and eventually the alternative rock movement.

passages.title: List of rock genres

passages.title: Art of representation

passages.title: Art of representation

passages.title: Art of representation

passages.title: Stanislavski's system
passages.text: Stanislavski's system is a systematic approach to training actors that the Russian theatre practitioner Konstantin Stanislavski developed in the first half of the 20th century.

passages.title: Stanislavski's system
passages.text: Stanislavski was the first in the West to propose that actor training should involve something more than merely physical and vocal training.

passages.title: Stanislavski's system
passages.text: His system cultivates what he calls the "art of experiencing" (with which he contrasts the "art of representation").

passages.title: Stanislavski's system
passages.text: It mobilises the actor's conscious thought and will in order to activate other, less-controllable psychological processes—such as emotional experience and subconscious behaviour—sympathetically and indirectly.

passages.title: Stanislavski's system

passages.title: Psycho-physical Awareness

passages.title: Psycho-physical Awareness
passages.text: This technique works on the relationship between the mind and the body and at developing an actor’s conscious awareness.

passages.title: Psycho-physical Awareness
passages.text: In other words, recognizing the resulting sensory and mental states in reaction to physical stimuli.

passages.title: Psycho-physical Awareness
passages.text: The pioneer of this technique is Constantin Stanislavski who sought to overcome the divisions between “mind from body, knowledge from feeling, analysis from action” through psychophysical training or the method of physical action, but it was Michael Chekhov who further developed an original and dependable method of what we now know to be psycho-physical awareness.

passages.title: Method acting
